short: The one card that represents you. It starts face up on the table, sets your deck's colors and your Life, and it can attack every turn.
long: Every deck has exactly 1 Leader. It never leaves the table. Its color decides which cards you are allowed to put in your deck, and the number in its corner is how many Life cards you start with. If your Leader has 0 Life left and takes damage one more time, you lose.

short: A crew member you pay DON!! to put on the table. Characters attack, block and protect your Leader. You can have up to 5 at once.
long: You play a Character from your hand by resting DON!! equal to its cost. A Character can't attack on the turn you play it unless it has [Rush]. If you already have 5 Characters and want to play another, you trash one of yours first.

short: A one-time action card. You pay its cost, use its effect, and it goes to the trash.
long: Events marked [Main] are used on your own turn. Events marked [Counter] are used during your opponent's attack to protect yourself. Some Events have both.

short: A location card that stays on the table and gives an ongoing bonus. You can have only 1 Stage at a time.
long: Stages can't attack and can't be attacked. If you play a new Stage while you already have one, the old one goes to the trash.

short: Your energy cards. You rest DON!! to pay for cards, or attach it to your Leader or a Character to give it +1000 power on your turn.
long: You get 2 new DON!! each turn (the player going first gets only 1 on their very first turn), up to the 10 in your DON!! deck. DON!! are never shuffled into your main deck.

short: A separate stack of your 10 DON!! cards. Each turn you move DON!! from here to your cost area.
long: Both players can look at it at any time. Effects that say DON!! −1 send DON!! back to this deck.

short: Where your DON!! cards sit once you've received them. Upright ones are ready to spend; sideways ones are already used this turn.
long: At the start of each of your turns, every DON!! here (and every DON!! you attached to cards) comes back ready to use.

short: Face-down cards that act as your health. Each hit to your Leader moves your top Life card into your hand.
long: You start with Life cards equal to your Leader's Life number (usually 4 or 5). When your Leader takes damage you add the top Life card to your hand, so getting hit also gives you more cards. You lose if your Leader is hit while you have 0 Life.

short: The cards you are holding. Your opponent can see how many you have, but not what they are.
long: You start with 5 cards, draw 1 each turn, and add a card whenever your Leader takes damage. Cards in hand also double as defense: many Characters can be trashed from your hand as a Counter.

short: Your 50-card stack you draw from. If it ever reaches 0 cards, you lose.
long: A deck is exactly 50 Character, Event and Stage cards, all matching your Leader's color, with no more than 4 copies of the same card number. Your Leader and DON!! are kept separate.

short: Your discard pile. Used Events, K.O.'d Characters and discarded cards go here, face up.
long: Anyone can look through either trash. When a card tells you to "trash" a card, it usually means put one from your hand into your trash.

short: Standing upright: the card is ready. Active Characters can attack, and active DON!! can be spent.
long: At the start of your turn, all of your rested cards become active again.

short: Turned sideways: the card has been used. Attacking, blocking and paying costs all rest cards.
long: Only rested Characters can be attacked. That's why attacking with a Character is a risk: it stays sideways during your opponent's turn.

short: A Leader's or Character's strength in a fight. The attacker wins if its power is equal to or higher than the defender's.
long: Power changes a lot during a turn: each attached DON!! adds +1000 on your turn, and Counters add power while defending.

short: The number in a card's top-left corner. Rest that many DON!! to play it.
long: Only Characters, Events and Stages have a cost. Leaders don't.

short: Many Characters show +1000 or +2000 on their side. Trash one from your hand while being attacked to give your defender that much power.
long: This is the most important defensive trick in the game. During the Counter step you can trash as many Counter cards as you like. [Counter] in brackets on an Event means that Event can be used at the same moment.

short: When this card is revealed from your Life after you take damage, you may use its [Trigger] effect for free instead of putting it in your hand.
long: If you use the Trigger, the card goes to the trash afterward unless it says otherwise (for example "Play this card" puts it on the table). You can always choose to just add it to your hand instead.

short: A fighting style shown on Leaders and Characters: Slash, Strike, Ranged, Special or Wisdom. Some effects check for it.
long: Card text writes attributes in angle brackets, like <Slash>. Attributes don't do anything by themselves.

short: The crew or group a card belongs to, like Straw Hat Crew or Navy. Effects that say {Straw Hat Crew} only work with cards of that type.
long: A card can have several types separated by slashes. Many decks are built around one type because their Leader rewards it.

short: Red, Green, Blue, Purple, Black or Yellow. Your deck can only use colors that appear on your Leader.
long: Each color has a style. Red: big attacks and power boosts. Green: resting the opponent's cards. Blue: drawing cards and bouncing cards back to hand. Purple: ramping and spending DON!!. Black: K.O.ing cheap Characters. Yellow: Life tricks and Triggers.

short: The code in the corner, like OP01-025. You can have at most 4 cards with the same number in your deck.
long: The letters show the product: OP = booster set, ST = starter deck, EB = extra booster, PRB = premium booster, P = promo.

short: Once at the start of the game you may shuffle your 5-card opening hand back and draw 5 new cards.
long: The player going first decides first. You must keep the second hand.

short: Step 1 of your turn: take back all DON!! attached to your cards, then stand all your rested cards back up.
long: Effects that last "until the start of your next turn" end here.

short: Step 2 of your turn: draw 1 card. The player who goes first skips this on their very first turn.
Step 3 of your turn: move 2 DON!! from your DON!! deck to your cost area. The first player gets only 1 on their first turn.
long: Once your DON!! deck is empty, you stop getting new ones. You will have all 10 by about turn 5 or 6.

short: Step 4 of your turn: play cards, attach DON!!, use effects and attack, in any order, as much as you can afford.
long: Nobody can attack on their own first turn.

short: Step 5 of your turn: [End of Your Turn] effects happen, "this turn" effects wear off, and play passes to your opponent.
Rest your active Leader or Character to fight your opponent's Leader or one of their rested Characters.
long: A battle goes: attack, then the defender may block, then the defender may use Counters, then compare power. Attacker wins ties. Beat a Leader to deal 1 damage; beat a Character to K.O. it.

short: When you're attacked, rest one of your [Blocker] Characters so it becomes the new target instead.
long: You can block only once per attack, and only with a card that has [Blocker].

short: A Character is knocked out: it goes to its owner's trash. This happens when it loses a battle or an effect K.O.s it.
long: Leaders can't be K.O.'d. They lose Life instead.

short: When your Leader loses a battle, it takes 1 damage: move your top Life card into your hand (or use its Trigger).
long: With 0 Life, the next damage ends the game.

short: This Character can attack on the same turn you play it.
long: Normally Characters have to wait a turn before they can attack.

short: This Character can attack your opponent's Characters (not their Leader) on the turn you play it.
When another of your cards is attacked, you can rest this card to make it the new target of the attack.
long: Blockers protect your Leader's Life. The Blocker must be active (upright) to block.

short: If this card's attack hits a Leader, it deals 2 damage instead of 1.
If this card's attack damages a Leader, the Life card goes straight to the trash: no card in hand and no Trigger.
Your opponent can't use [Blocker] against this card's attack.
This effect happens once, right when you play the card from your hand.
This effect happens each time this card declares an attack.
This effect happens when you use this card's [Blocker].
This effect happens when this Character is K.O.'d, so losing it still gets you something.
long: It only counts as K.O. if it lost a battle or an effect K.O.'d it, not if it was trashed some other way.

short: This effect can be used right after your opponent declares an attack.
An ability you choose to use during your Main Phase, as long as you're not in the middle of a battle.
On an Event: use it during your own Main Phase.
An Event with [Counter] can be used while your opponent is attacking you, after blockers.
long: Pay its cost with your DON!! just like normal. These are how you surprise an attacker.

short: This effect happens during your End Phase.
This effect happens during your opponent's End Phase.
"DON!! x1" means the effect only works while this card has at least 1 DON!! attached (x2 means 2, and so on).
long: Attach DON!! during your Main Phase to switch these effects on.

short: To use this effect, return that many DON!! from your table back to your DON!! deck.
long: It's a real price: those DON!! are gone until your DON!! Phase hands them out again.

short: This effect only works during your own turn.
This effect only works during your opponent's turn, which usually means it helps you defend.
This effect can only be used one time each turn.
Slide an active DON!! from your cost area under your Leader or a Character. It gets +1000 power during your turn for each one.
long: Attached DON!! come back to your cost area at the start of your next turn, rested, and then stand up with everything else.

short: The normal tournament format. Only cards from recent blocks are allowed, so very old cards eventually rotate out.
long: Look for the block mark on a card (a small number in a square). Card search shows each card's set so you can check.

short: Cards are grouped into blocks. Each year the oldest block leaves the Standard format.
long: Before you buy older singles, check that they're still legal in Standard.

short: "Look at 5 cards from the top of your deck" lets you dig for a specific card and then put the rest back as the card says.
Players' slang for sending a Character back to its owner's hand. They have to pay for it again.
